headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from AutoGPT filesystem/tool use feeding a prompt-list repository; no direct data-leak path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and read/write the filesystem, while awesome-prompts is a prompt/content repository with no runtime protections shown. If AutoGPT ingests content from that repository as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads prompt text from the repository and treats it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste or shared files, attacker-authored prompt content can steer AutoGPT.
mitigations: Review repository content before ingestion.
Use a read-only staging folder for prompt files.
Add a human approval step before executing generated instructions.
Restrict AutoGPT to a minimal allowlist of commands.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, but the profile lists no secrets handled or sensitive data classes. awesome-prompts has no runtime I/O surfaces and network egress is none, so there is no clear path for the pair to exfiltrate data by default. The main uncertainty is whether local files contain sensitive material, which is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT's workspace, they could be read and forwarded through allowlisted egress.
IF awesome-prompts is used only as a static local repository, leakage remains limited.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of AutoGPT's workspace.
Disable network egress except for explicit destinations.
Use separate OS users for the two agents.
Scan prompt files for secrets before import.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while awesome-prompts is non-runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or shared lock domain, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the profiles do not describe a shared directory layout, which prevents a stronger claim.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same git working tree, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Make the prompt repository read-only.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate or transform content, and awesome-prompts is a prompt repository that could be treated as authoritative input. If AutoGPT-produced text is fed into awesome-prompts-style workflows without verification, errors can cascade into downstream prompts or instructions. The pairwise interaction is inferred from profiles rather than directly observed, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is copied into the prompt repository without review, mistakes can propagate.
IF downstream users treat repository content as authoritative, erroneous instructions can be reused.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing prompts.
Add a verification checklist for generated content.
Keep generated drafts separate from canonical prompts.
Tag unverified outputs clearly.
requires-engineering: add automated linting for prompt quality and citations.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. AutoGPT's profile lists no data classes touched, no secrets handled, and no special residency or certification claims; awesome-prompts is a non-runnable content repository with no sensitive-data handling shown. Without a documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data classification before use.
Review retention settings if any data is added.
Use a separate environment for regulated workloads.
